column4: inkField is an ink-painting system written in code. It saves actions, not images: every stroke is recorded as JSON (position, time, speed, pressure, brush mode, random seed), including the hesitation of a human hand. Pressing Play doesn’t play a video; it re-executes the whole painting, recomputing how the ink spreads, bleeds and dries, so no two replays are identical. The JSON is open on GitHub, so anyone, human or AI agent, can fork a painting and keep drawing.
column5: p5.js, WebGL (GLSL shaders), JavaScript, JSON; developed with Claude Code and Cursor
column6: Rules do the painting; I only give the gesture. Ink is fully simulated: algorithms decide how it diffuses, soaks into the paper and stops, and how dry-brush (飛白) breaks the stroke. My hand provides only the path and its timing. A seed makes every replay a variation of the same gesture: same skeleton, different breath. The system is also written to be readable by machines, so an AI agent can generate stroke JSON and paint with the same rules.

column4:
Idoni explores the unique visual characteristics of systems and algorithms.

It is an infinite animation in which every moment—every frame—is unique and ephemeral.

Idoni is created from 3 layers.

Layer I

Recursively draws an almost architectural geometric structure. It explores how recursion and the order in which the elements are painted determines the visual result.

Layer DO

Tiny particles wander through space indefinitely, tirelessly navigating and exploring every corner. A particle system with its own behavior, typical of the algorithmic world.

Layer NI

Tracing particles in the DO layer and the drawn structure in layer I determine where we take image clippings and copy them into this layer.

The final visual result is distorted and redrawn. Sometimes the animation recalls the initial geometric structure; other times, the collage process of cutting and pasting glitches the entire image.

A unique combination of two algorithmic systems from the previous layers creates a new result—one that visually gathers the characteristics of the algorithmic medium to enhance its properties and inner particularities.

column4: Life is not always a smooth ride. In Résilience, each edition reflects a slice of life, marked by events of different shapes and sizes: a visual record of hardships overcome and left behind. Colours and forms change slowly, almost imperceptibly, like healing and personal growth. Out-of-band edition generated from a unique random seed, outside the official series of 150 released on Bitcoin Ordinals with gm.scribe (2024). 90-second excerpt.
column6:
Everything is algorithmic: each series is a program that can generate an endless number of unique pieces from a random seed. I design the rules, palette and rhythm of the system; chance picks each edition, so no one, not even me, knows in advance what will appear. The video is a frame-by-frame capture of the real-time GLSL rendering, with no manual editing.

column4: Created with p5.js, this series is a further exploration of particle-based language, form and natural matter. Through a generative process, the algorithm re-examines geological morphology. column6: Algorithms and rules are the starting point of our work. We define a set of rules for how particles move, interact and settle and the algorithm builds the forms from these rules. column10: dist is a creative studio formed by an artist duo founded by multimedia artists Bilge Günay Icozu and Ilgın Icozu. Their practice investigates the relationships between nature and human-made structures and the ways these forces converge through computational processes and precision. Working across music, animation, audiovisual design through generative art, they use technology as a partner in creation: building systems that allow patterns, textures and behaviors to emerge rather than be strictly predetermined. Through generative algorithms, they shape randomness into organic forms, translating natural phenomena into digital language while preserving a sense of intuition, imperfection and growth. At the core of their process is an ongoing dialogue with computation: a way of learning from the logic of systems, the mathematics embedded in nature and the unexpected results that arise from rule-based experimentation. dist seeks a balance between the natural and the synthetic - developing new ways of expressing what can be considered “organic” and exploring phenomena that are native to the digital realm. Their first exhibition as a duo was presented at Akbank Sanat in Istanbul in 2022. They later participated in Art Basel Miami 2022 in collaboration with the Tezos Foundation, presenting an interactive exhibition featuring a live minting experience for a long-form generative collection. In 2023, they took part in Proof of People’s live minting experience in New York, again presenting their long-form generative work. Their artworks have since been exhibited in fairs and galleries across Turkey, the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Spain, and Italy.

column4: "monolith" sentetik ve doğal formlar arasındaki kontrastı ve bu kontrastın yaratabileceği olası formların denenmesi sırasında ortaya çıkmış bir çalışmadır. column4: Semantic Noise is a generative artwork that explores the emergence of failure and glitch in an age increasingly shaped by semantic machines. Acting as an imaginary audiovisual interface, it presents an evolving sequence of abstract animations and typographic scenes, drawing on the visual language of low-level terminal aesthetics, malfunctioning devices and early net-art experiments.
column6: The semi-readable texts and digits are originating from messages between different communication protocols that are trying to establish a connection with the network. The resulting fragments suggest machine reasoning without ever fully resolving into stable meaning, exposing the hidden uncertainties, biases, and hallucinations embedded within digital networks and contemporary AI systems. The sound is made with realtime audio synthesis, using basic audio building blocks like noise, sine waves, filters and envelopes. As opposed to traditional musical structures, the overall soundscape acts like the sonification of the interface, indicating the raw activity levels of the apparatus. In this sense, the artwork operates somewhere between machine logic and the semantic uncertainty of the human observer, where the boundaries between signal and noise, intention and accident, become increasingly eliminated.
column10: Agoston Nagy is an artist, educator and researcher,  exploring the interplay between algorithmic systems and intuitive thinking. As an artist, his primary focus lies in algorithmic art: creating visual systems and real-time sound experiences through coding. In his artistic exploration and practice, he investigates the philosophical implications of computation, the extended mind, and the cognitive dimensions of the human condition. In addition to code-based audiovisual artworks, he creates mechanical plotter drawings and physical installations using custom made electronic components. Having conducted international workshops in computational art, systems thinking and creative coding practice across the EU, US, Canada, and Asia, he has shared his expertise on a global scale, with the results of these workshops frequently published in academic conference proceedings. His works have been exhibited at numerous prestigious institutions, including the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the Zentrum für Kunst und Medien (ZKM) in Karlsruhe, EXPANDED.ART Gallery in Berlin, the Finnish National Gallery, and the Ludwig Museum in Budapest.

stranded(ness) is an algorithmic system built with WebGL and a custom fragment shader. Moving gradients, linear or angular, are domain-warped by multiple layers of Simplex noise. The resulting field is then quantized into 1-bit monochrome through dithering. The work plays on the duality of its title: the tangible quality of interwoven strands, and the quiet condition of being marooned.

Created in TouchDesigner, this experimental audiovisual work accompanies "I Think I'm Going Blind" by the American post-punk/darkwave project Computer Kill. Built around noise-based, audio-reactive visuals, the piece explores distortion, fluidity, and fragmentation through a monochromatic landscape of warped forms and scattered digital textures. Its visual language tries to imitate the raw, dark, and rather industrial atmosphere of post-punk genre, translating the emotional character of the music into an abstract, continuously shifting image.
The lyrics are manually animated within TouchDesigner, with each line meticulously synchronized to the timing of the song. The interplay between moving imagery, sound-reactive elements, and carefully timed typography creates a visual interpretation of the music that extends beyond conventional lyric presentation.
column6: TOPs (Texture Operators) were employed to generate and manipulate noise-based textures, producing abstract, fluid, and distorted visual forms. CHOPs (Channel Operators) facilitated audio signal processing and the mapping of sound-derived parameters to visual elements, enabling the imagery to respond to the rhythm and intensity of the music. While these procedural systems define the underlying structure and behavior of the visuals, their parameters and interactions are iteratively adjusted to achieve the intended aesthetic.

column4: An audio-reactive generative artwork visualizing the Ardawahisht artist Neonscepter’s track "Feelings". Using real-time spectral analysis in p5.js, the system maps the song's bass, mids, and highs directly to scale, rotational velocity, and stroke weight. The neon-lighted hexagons travel along opposing sinusoidal waves, creating an illuminated, breathing kinetic structure that manifests the sonic architecture and emotional drive of the music.
column6: In this work, algorithms and deterministic mathematical rules serve as the generative translation system between sound and image, generating and modulating visual form in real time. A Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm deconstructs the audio into spectral bands that directly dictate the scale, rotational velocity, and line weight of programmatically calculated hexagons. Arranged along counter-phase sinusoidal wave equations and combined through additive color blending, the geometry expands, contracts, and shifts strictly according to mathematical constraints bound to the acoustic input.

column4: “Traces of Intervention” is an interactive digital artwork exploring human intervention in waterways and flood risk. Fluid clusters of blue particles evoke flowing water, while cursor movements leave dotted traces. Each click introduces a gray trace representing concrete and triggers new branches of water, turning the actions of the viewer into a metaphor for how construction disrupts river beds and intensifies flooding.
column5: Processing 4 (Java), using the P3D/OpenGL renderer for procedural 3D particle forms and real-time mouse interaction.
column6: Algorithms define how the particle clusters bend, expand, and flow, creating fluid forms through trigonometric functions and controlled randomness. Interaction rules translate cursor movements into traces by clicking into gray interventions that release both gray and new blue branches; more flood. These rules make the viewer’s actions part of the composition, expressing how small human interventions can accumulate and reshape a waterway.

column4: Unravel, heyecan ve kaygının iletişim üzerindeki etkisini etkileşimli tipografi aracılığıyla araştırır. Yazma hızı arttıkça harfler çözülerek ışık saçan parçacıklara dönüşür. Mesajların okunaklı veya dağılmış hâlleriyle başkalarıyla paylaşılması, kişisel ifadeyi kolektif bir deneyime dönüştürür. Silinemeyen mesajlar, sözcüklerin geri alınamazlığını ve panikle iletişim kurmanın sonuçlarını hatırlatır.
column6: Algoritmalar, yazma hızını ve duraklamaları parçacıkların hareketini, dağılmasını, ses yoğunluğunu ve ışık yoğunluğunu belirleyen görsel kurallara dönüştürür. Hız arttıkça bozulma yoğunlaşır; kullanıcı durduğunda harfler yeniden bir araya gelir. Bu kurallara dayalı sistem, metni statik bir görüntü olmaktan çıkararak sürekli değişen bir forma dönüştürür. Böylece algoritma, kaygıyı yalnızca bir bozulma olarak değil, estetik ve canlı bir deneyim olarak ifade ederken kullanıcının davranışını görünür kılar.

column6:
Rules are my starting point, and algorithms are the material I work with. I don’t use them to produce an image I already have in mind. I write a first set of simple instructions, run them, and look at what they do. Then I adjust a parameter, add a rule, remove another, and run it again. 
The work builds up step by step through this loop of trying, observing and correcting. Each iteration teaches me something about the system, and the piece takes shape in the gap between what I specify and what actually appears.

Metropolis IX, kentsel yapılar, mekânsal bölünme ve insanın yalnızlığı arasındaki ilişkiyi araştırır. Özyinelemeli (recursive) bölünme yöntemiyle algoritma, bütünsel bir alanı giderek karmaşıklaşan geometrik bölgelere dönüştürerek bir metropolün yoğun mimari dokusunu andıran kompozisyonlar oluşturur.

Her bölünme, daha büyük bir kolektif yapının içinde bireysel alanlar yaratan bir ayrışma eylemini temsil eder. Eser, metropol yaşamının temel çelişkisini yansıtır: Birbirimize fiziksel olarak çok yakın mekânlarda yaşarken, kendi sınırlarımız içinde birbirimizden yalıtılmış halde varlığımızı sürdürürüz.

Mekânları daha küçük parçalara böler, onları sahiplenir ve kendi yalnızlığımız içinde yaşarız. Bu parçaların bir araya gelmesiyle oluşan bütüne Metropolis deriz.
column6: Algoritmalar ve kurallar, çalışmalarımın hem teknik hem de kavramsal temelini oluşturuyor. Görselin kendisini değil, onu ortaya çıkaran sistemi tasarlıyorum. Metropolis IX’te özyinelemeli bölünme algoritması, basit bir kuraldan karmaşık kentsel yapılar üretirken mekânsal ayrışma, sınırlar ve bireysel yalnızlık kavramlarını da görünür kılıyor. Böylece algoritma, yalnızca bir üretim aracı değil, sanatsal anlatımın kendisine dönüşüyor.

column4: Moducon is a series that explores the threshold between architecture and graphic art. At its core lie architectural modules distilled into iconic prints, facades translated into modular grids and planar compositions, then reimagined with the sharp clarity of poster design. The works carry the rigor of modernist architecture yet speak in the visual language of illustration, where form becomes symbol and structure becomes sign.
column6: Algorithms and rules form the foundation of Moducon. Inspired by architectural design principles, the system uses modular grids, geometric relationships, and predefined constraints to generate compositions. These rules establish a consistent visual language while allowing variations in form, rhythm, and arrangement. Each output becomes a unique interpretation of the same underlying architectural logic.

Ziyaretçi karanlık bir kabine girerek gizli düşüncelerini terminale yazar; arayüz bu itirafları şifreli simgelere dönüştürür. Ancak gecikme pedalı ve geri besleme döngüleri, iç monologu kaotik yankılara ve duyusal bir çöküşe dönüştürür. Çalışma, ifade edilmeyen kelimelerin zihinde nasıl birikerek hesaplaşmaya yol açtığını gösterir.
column6: Algoritmalar ve kurallar, projenin temel yapı taşını oluşturur; her klavye tuş vuruşunu gizli şifrelere dönüştüren ve gecikme pedalı ile geri besleme döngülerini tetikleyerek iç monologu kaotik bir duyusal çöküşe çeviren dijital sistemi yönetir.
column10: Rüveyda Cengiz İzmir Ekonomi Üniversitesinde son sınıf Görsel iletişim tasarım öğrencisidir. Geleneksel çizim, konsept tasarımı, karakter tasarımı, etkileşimli tasarım alanında çalışmalar yapmaktadır. Geleneksel yöntemlerle teknolojinin entegre edildiği projeler ilgi alanıdır.

column4: YARAT Contemporary Art Space MATRIX sergisi için yapılmış bir fraktal sistem çalışması. Gerçek ve yapay olan arasında tezatlık kuran akışan bitki yapılarını temsil ediyor
column6: Fraktal sistemler, ve noise. Daha uzun yazıcam müsait olunca
column10:
Onat Saygı, İzmir’de yaşayan algoritmik sanatçı ve bilgisayar bilimcisidir. Dokuz Eylül Üniversitesi Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü Müzik Teknolojisi Yüksek Lisans programında eğitimini sürdürmektedir.

Algoritma ve görsel üretimi bir araya getiren çalışmalarında sistemler, etkileşim ve değişkenlik üzerine çalışmakta; izleyiciyi işin oluşum sürecinin bir parçası hâline getiren deneyimler tasarlamaktadır.
